properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 8:35PM MDT until October 26 at 1:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Catastrophic flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected along the San Juan River between Four Corners and Mexican
Hat. This is an emergency situation!

* WHERE...Western Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding along San Juan River is occurring with major
flooding forecast. Low-water crossing are inundated with water and
may not be passable. The river is running fast and high. Do not
attempt to cross.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 830 PM MDT, Major flooding is expected to occur along the San
Juan River from Four Corners to Mexican Hat. The San Juan River
is forecast to crest around midnight tonight at the Four Corners,
reaching Montezuma Creek around 5 am MDT Sunday, cresting between
Bluff and Mexican Hat Sunday afternoon and peaking at Mexican Hat
by 5 pm Sunday evening around 36 feet which will exceed all time
record levels. The San Juan River will rise above flood stage
Sunday morning and continue to rise Sunday afternoon to moderate
flood stage, peaking above major flood stage at Mexican Hat by 5
pm Sunday evening.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
San Juan River
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mexican Hat, Tselakai Dezza, Bluff, Halchita, Montezuma Creek and
Aneth.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 2:46PM MST until October 26 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues. This
rainfall occurred on Wednesday and Thursday.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST Sunday Night /100 AM MDT Monday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is occurring.
Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 240 PM MST /340 PM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall this evening. However, downstream
impacts will continue at Navajo Route 71 to Birdsprings through
at least Sunday.
- Flooding is occurring along the Little Colorado River.
- For Little Colorado at Winslow:
At 2:00pm MST /3:00pm MDT/ the stage was 18.34 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: The river is cresting now and is forecast to fall
through this evening.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:30AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall to 12.0 feet this afternoon. It
will then rise to 12.5 feet this evening. It will fall to 11.9
feet just after midnight tonight. It will then rise to 14.2 feet
Saturday morning. It will fall again and remain below flood
stage.
- Action stage is 13.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.
